newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tutu to meet S.Africa's P.W. Botha in truth probe.
newsitem.headline: Tutu to meet S.Africa's P.W. Botha in truth probe.

text.p: Archbishop Desmond Tutu, who is heading a Truth Commission on human rights under apartheid, said he would meet South Africa's last hardline white ruler privately on Thursday.

Tutu, chairman of the statutory Truth and Reconciliation Commission, said in a statement he would meet the 80-year-old former president at an undisclosed venue near Botha's retirement home in Wilderness.
"At Mr Botha's request and with my agreement the media will not be present," Tutu said, adding that he would address a news conference in Cape Town later in the day.
Botha has been implicated in the planning of a violent 1980s government campaign against anti-apartheid groups aligned to Nelson Mandela's then-banned African National Congress (ANC).

Tutu's commission has until the end of next year to unravel the human rights record of the war over apartheid, to pardon human rights offenders on both sides of the struggle and to award limited compensation to victims.
Botha, whose government was dominated by police and military programmes to contain the black uprising against white rule, has vowed never to apologise for his actions.
The former president was partially disabled by a stroke early in 1989 and resigned a few months later when F.W. de Klerk launched a cabinet coup and then went on to repudiate and dismantle apartheid.
The truth probe was included in terms negotiated by de Klerk and Mandela for the 1994 transfer of power from the white minority to an elected majority government.
